colorRules.accentUsage: The accent #C2410C is a spotlight, never a wash. Use it on the primary button, the active nav item, the active segmented control in the composer, and as a 3px left border on rows flagged urgent. It appears only on elements that represent the user's next best action or a critical state. Do not use accent as a background fill for cards, tables, or empty states; never apply it to icons just for decoration.
colorRules.semanticUsage: Semantic colors are reserved for status and priority signaling: destructive (red) for urgent/overdue timers and destructive actions, warning (yellow) for pending/attention, success (green) for open/in-progress, info (blue) for new. They appear as badge backgrounds (pale tints) and text, never as large surface colors.
colorRules.neutralUsage: Neutrals carry the chrome: backgrounds (bg-background, bg-muted, bg-card), borders, and text are the default for the interface. All structural surfaces are neutral. The sidebar, topbar, table rows, and cards stay muted; tactile hierarchy comes from borders and shadows, not from color.
forbiddenPatterns: Accent washes: no translucent or low-opacity accent backgrounds on tables, cards, or full-screen surfaces.
Gradient walls: no gradients behind headers, buttons, or content.
Rainbow badges: do not use more than one status/priority color in a single badge; badges must stay flat and single-purpose.
Decorative use of accent: no accent-colored avatars, icons, or borders for non-interactive, non-priority elements.

typographyRules.displayUsage: Space Grotesk is for display and wayfinding: the product name, page titles, conversation subject lines, dialog titles, and the numbers in SLA timers. It gives a technical, geometric voice that matches the triage deck idea.
typographyRules.bodyUsage: DM Sans carries all body text, UI controls, table cells, messages, navigation, and labels. It is the workhorse typeface for dense reading and scanning.
typographyRules.monoUsage: JetBrains Mono appears in ticket IDs, response timers, SLA countdowns, and any value where fixed-width alignment aids scanning. It is also used for the timer badge and the progress indicator text.
typographyRules.weightRules: Display titles use Space Grotesk 600; section subheads and card titles use Space Grotesk 500. Body uses DM Sans 400 for regular text and 500 for emphasis (names, active states, button labels). Mono uses 400 for timers and 500 for highlighted counts.
typographyRules.sizeRules: Keep a compact scale: body 14px, labels and meta 12px, table headers 12px with medium weight, input text 14px, page titles 20px, dialog titles 18px, empty state title 18px. Do not exceed 20px for any title in this dense UI.

spacingRules.sectionMargins: Use 16px gutters on page content. Sections within a screen (filters, table, thread, panel) are separated by 24px vertical margins. The sidebar is 256px wide and the topbar is 56px tall, maintaining a fixed chrome.
spacingRules.componentPadding: Compact and consistent: buttons 36px high with 12px horizontal padding; table rows 48px high with 12px cell padding; cards 16px padding; dialog 24px padding; badges 2px vertical / 8px horizontal.
spacingRules.rhythmDescription: Rhythm is intentionally uneven: 8px between badges, 12px between related actions, 16px between list and filters, 24px between major content blocks. This creates a tight, operational cadence that prioritizes scanning and quick action.

motionRules.transitions: Transitions apply to background-color, border-color, opacity, transform, and box-shadow. Use for hovered rows, active tabs, dropdowns, dialogs, and button states. Avoid animating layout properties.
motionRules.easing: Use the theme easing cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.0, 0, 1.0) — a fast, precise deceleration that feels responsive and calm.
motionRules.duration: Micro-interactions (hover, focus, button press) use 120ms. Element appearance (menus, dropdowns, badge updates) uses 200ms. Large overlays (dialog, full-screen transition) use 400ms.

signatureMoves: Priority light beam: urgent tickets get a 3px left border in the accent color plus a mono countdown timer in JetBrains Mono. The row edge becomes a signal.

Status chip trio: statuses appear as small, pale rounded chips (blue for new, green for open, yellow for pending) that stay muted but instantly scannable; priority badges are stronger solids. This contrast between soft status and bold priority creates calm precision.

Composer toggle: in conversation detail, the Reply / Internal Note segmented control uses the accent for the active mode, letting the user cast the message as either response or internal note before typing.
Micro-monos everywhere: every SLA timer and ticket ID is set in JetBrains Mono, often in muted gray, giving the board an instrumentation-readout feel.
antiPatterns: Stock shadcn look: no default violet accent, generic button styles, or unmodified component defaults. We replace with the orange spotlight and mono timers.
Accent washes: no translucent accent backgrounds on table rows, cards, or nav items. Use neutral grays for chrome and let accent be a deliberate highlight.
Gradient walls: no gradients on headers, buttons, or empty states.
Template copy: no placeholder lorem ipsum or generic toast text; use realistic support language and customer names that match the product's personality.
